finalResponse:
# Perpetual-to-Subscription Transition Plan

*Illustrative $200M model — License/upgrade $90M, Maintenance $80M (20% attach on a ~$400M net installed license base), Services $30M. Re-run with actuals; the structure, ratios, and decision rules are the transferable part.*

---

## Executive Summary (one page)

| Commitment | Target | Tripwire |
|---|---|---|
| **Trough depth** | Revenue bottoms at **~$143M in Year 2, −28% vs. baseline** | −33% triggers board review |
| **Trough duration** | **Two years down (Y1, Y2), recovery in Y3, above baseline in Y4** | Slip of >2 quarters triggers pause |
| **Conversion pace** | 15% / 35% / 60% / 80% / 92% of maintenance base cumulative, Y1–Y5 | <70% of plan for 2 quarters |
| **Retention floor** | **≥93% annual logo retention through the trough** (vs. ~94% today); absolute floor 90% | 2 consecutive quarters <92% |
| **Cash** | Peak cumulative FCF shortfall vs. run-rate **~$120M**; secure **$150M** liquidity (cash + undrawn revolver) before launch | Draw >$100M |
| **Exit state (Y5)** | **ARR ~$259M, NRR ≥110%, cloud ≥60% of ARR, subscription ≥90% of revenue** | Cloud mix <40% at Y3 |

**The four decisions this plan makes:**

1. **Decouple commercial change from technical change.** Sell recurring economics on the software customers already run. Do not make cloud re-platforming a condition of subscribing. Then use price escalators, feature differentiation, and migration subsidies — not a cheaper on-prem SKU — to pull the base to cloud on a paced schedule.
2. **Anchor conversion pricing to what customers pay today, not to a % of list.** Existing maintenance payers migrate at **1.15× current maintenance** and step to list over five years under a contractual cap. New-logo list is 35% of perpetual equivalent; that number never applies to a converting customer on day one.
3. **Buy retention with entitlement protection, not discounts.** A published Customer Bill of Rights — perpetual rights *suspended, not terminated*, with a revert option; no maintenance EOL inside 36 months; no forced re-platform — is cheaper and more effective than price concessions.
4. **Pre-commit the trough publicly and change the scoreboard before the first bad quarter,** including executive incentive comp. Boards and investors tolerate a trough they were sold; they do not tolerate one they discover.

---

## 0. Day 0–30: Diagnose the Competitor Failure Before Copying the Cure

We do not know why the competitor lost a fifth of its base. The countermeasures differ sharply by cause, so this is a two-week, funded workstream, not an assumption.

| Hypothesis | Diagnostic | If true, countermeasure |
|---|---|---|
| Price shock (annual spend jumped 50–100%) | Reconstruct their maintenance→subscription price delta from public price lists, reseller quotes, defector interviews | Longer ramp, hard uplift cap, cohort-segmented pricing |
| Forced support EOL | Their published EOL notices vs. defection timing | 36-month minimum EOL notice, feature-frozen maintenance track |
| Cloud gating (subscribe = re-platform) | Defector cloud-readiness profile | Term on-prem bridge SKU (core of this plan) |
| Entitlement/ownership objection | Win/loss interviews, procurement/legal objections | Suspension-not-termination, escrow, revert rights |
| Channel revolt (partners lost margin) | Partner-program change history, partner defections | Recurring-margin partner model designed pre-launch |

**Deliverables by Day 14:** defector cohort analysis, 15–20 win/loss interviews (their lost customers, our sales team's competitive notes), 5 channel-partner debriefs, and a one-page "failure mode" memo that gates final pricing approval.

---

## 1. Strategic Frame: Three Separable Transitions

Failed conversions bundle three distinct changes into one event: **commercial** (perpetual+maintenance → recurring), **technical** (on-prem → vendor-hosted), and **contractual** (ownership → right-to-use). Each carries independent customer risk. Bundled, they compound into "you are taking away what I bought, raising my price, and forcing me to re-platform" — a defensible reason to run a competitive evaluation.

**We separate them.** Commercial conversion runs on the customer's current deployment. Technical migration runs on a separate, incentivized, customer-paced track.

**The unmanaged downside of decoupling** — and we name it explicitly — is that a comfortable, permanent on-prem term license gives us ARR optics without cloud's gross-margin, release-velocity, or COGS benefits, while we carry dual engineering and support cost structures forever. Four forcing functions prevent that (§2).

---

## 2. Offer Architecture

Three product lines through the trough, tiered for expansion.

### A. Cloud Subscription — the strategic SKU

Vendor-hosted, continuous release, tiered so that migration does not freeze the account's price forever:

| Tier | Scope | Annual price (% of equivalent perpetual list) |
|---|---|---|
| Essentials | Core module, standard support | **~26%** |
| Professional | Core + 3 modules, API access, premium support | **~35%** |
| Enterprise | All modules + new cloud-only capabilities, SSO/governance, guaranteed SLA | **~45%** |

**Expansion vectors designed before migration, because a migrated base cannot be re-priced:** seats, environments/instances, API-call or compute consumption tiers, module attach, premium support tier. Target ≥30% of ARR growth from installed-base expansion by Y3. Flat "all modules included" pricing is explicitly rejected — it discounts our largest accounts and raises price on our smallest, and it eliminates the NRR engine that determines the post-trough multiple.

### B. Term License, On-Prem — the bridge SKU

Customer-managed, same binaries, 1–3 year renewable license + support. For regulated, air-gapped, sovereignty-constrained, and change-averse accounts. **Deliberately priced at parity or above cloud:**

- List = **cloud Professional list (35%)**, with a **contractual +6% annual escalator**
- Support tier is **N-1 release cadence**; cloud-only capabilities are not backported
- **Closed to new logos at end of Year 3**; renewal-only thereafter
- Migration credits and free professional-services subsidy make cloud *cheaper in practice* — we steer with incentives, never with a lower list price on the SKU we intend to retire

### C. Legacy Maintenance — grandfathered, feature-frozen

Existing perpetual holders may stay on maintenance at current terms with **published, contractual EOL dates no sooner than 36 months out**, on a feature-frozen version stream: security patches, platform certifications, and critical bug fixes only. Maintenance uplift capped at CPI+2% through the transition. This is the "we are not forcing you" proof point, and it is worth more in retention than any discount.

### Revenue-recognition design (decide before launch, with the auditor)

Under ASC 606, a functional-IP term license typically recognizes the license component **at a point in time**, with support ratable. A 3-year term license would therefore produce an upfront spike and a two-year cliff — reproducing exactly the lumpiness investors already discount, inside the product we are selling as the cure.

Two responses, both required:

1. **Contract design.** Where the term license is bundled with unspecified, continuous updates such that the license is not separately beneficial without them, the combined performance obligation can qualify for over-time recognition. This is a deliberate, documented, auditable design choice — **engage the audit partner in the design phase, not at the first close.** Target: ratable recognition on ≥80% of bridge-SKU bookings.
2. **Metric framing.** For whatever remains point-in-time, the investor plan leads with ARR, cRPO, and RPO, and publishes a **GAAP-to-ARR bridge every quarter** (§5). Otherwise we trade one bad optic for another.

---

## 3. Migration Offer for Existing License Holders

### 3.1 The Customer Bill of Rights (published, contractual)

The entitlement problem is solved with rights, not rebates:

1. **Perpetual rights are suspended, not terminated.** On subscribing, the perpetual license is placed in contractual suspension. If the customer non-renews, perpetual rights to the last version they were entitled to **automatically revert**, with a paid re-instatement path to maintenance at then-current rates. They never lose the asset they bought.
2. **Binary and source escrow** available on request (Enterprise tier, or paid add-on) for customers with continuity mandates.
3. **No forced re-platform.** Subscription is available on-prem indefinitely for existing holders.
4. **No removal of purchased functionality.** Anything they own today remains available in their subscription scope at no incremental charge.
5. **Minimum 36-month EOL notice** on any support stream, published on a public roadmap page.
6. **Uplift cap:** contractual maximum annual increase (see ramp below) for the life of the initial term plus one renewal.

### 3.2 Conversion pricing — the "Loyalty Ramp"

A maintenance-paying customer pays **20% of license per year today**. Moving them to 35% list is a **75% increase in annual spend** — that, more than the ownership question, is what drives mass defection. So:

| Year of subscription | Price as multiple of their prior maintenance | Effective % of license |
|---|---|---|
| Y1 | **1.15×** | 23% |
| Y2 | 1.15× | 23% |
| Y3 | 1.35× | 27% |
| Y4 | 1.55× | 31% |
| Y5 → steady state | 1.75× (= list) | 35% |

- **Price-lock guarantee:** the ramp is contractual for 5 years; no uplift exceeds 20% in any year, and Y1–Y2 are locked flat.
- Ramp applies to the **scope they own**. Any expansion (seats, modules, tiers) is priced at list — this is where expansion revenue comes from, and it is not discounted.
- **Cloud migration credit:** customers who move to cloud within 24 months hold their ramp position and receive **professional-services migration at 50% subsidy** (capped at 15% of first-year ACV). After 24 months, subsidy drops to 25%, then zero.

### 3.3 The Ownership Equity Credit — for lapsed-maintenance customers only

Roughly 25–30% of the installed base pays no maintenance. They are the highest-defection-risk cohort and cost nothing today. For them only:

- **Credit of 20% of net license fees paid**, applied against subscription fees, capped at 30% of the annual fee in any year, expiring after 4 years.
- Not offered to maintenance-current customers — they get the Loyalty Ramp instead. Stacking both would deepen the trough materially for no incremental retention.

### 3.4 Cohort segmentation — one offer will overpay some and lose others

| Cohort | ~% of base value | Motion | Offer variant |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Top 50 accounts** | ~45% | Named exec sponsor, custom migration plan, quarterly business reviews | Ramp + 3-year price lock + co-designed cloud roadmap + advisory-board seat; negotiate multi-year prepay |
| **Mid-market (~600 accounts)** | ~35% | Campaign-driven, inside-sales-led, renewal-triggered | Standard Ramp, self-serve migration tooling, PS subsidy |
| **Long tail (~4,000 accounts)** | ~12% | Fully digital, no-touch | Ramp auto-applied at renewal, one-click accept, partner-delivered migration |
| **Lapsed maintenance** | ~8% recoverable | Win-back campaign | Ownership Equity Credit + amnesty on back maintenance |

**Sequencing rule:** never open a conversion conversation off-cycle. Every conversion is a **renewal-triggered** event, so the customer is already in a buying moment and the alternative (keep paying maintenance) is visibly available.

---

## 4. The Trough Model: Depth vs. Adoption

### 4.1 Base case

| ($M) | Y0 | Y1 | Y2 | Y3 | Y4 | Y5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Perpetual license/upgrade | 90 | 45 | 12 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| Maintenance (unconverted) | 80 | 68 | 48 | 28 | 14 | 6 |
| Subscription (recognized) | 0 | 17 | 53 | 102 | 161 | 225 |
| Services | 30 | 32 | 30 | 30 | 28 | 27 |
| **Total revenue** | **200** | **162** | **143** | **163** | **203** | **258** |
| **vs. baseline** | — | **−19%** | **−28%** | **−18%** | **+2%** | **+29%** |
| **Exit ARR** | 80* | 34 | 75 | 130 | 192 | 259 |
| FCF | 30 |
